entities.name: Viral Hemorrhagic Fevers
entities.description: A severe, life-threatening group of zoonotic viral syndromes caused by enveloped RNA viruses across four families (Filoviridae, Bunyavirales, Arenaviridae, Flaviviridae), characterized by abrupt fever, diffuse microvascular permeability, marked AST-dominant transaminitis, profound thrombocytopenia, consumptive coagulopathy, and shock.

entities.name: Abrupt High Fever
entities.description: Sudden dramatic onset of high continuous body temperature (>39°C) with shaking chills and rigors heralds acute viraemic dissemination.

entities.name: Prostrating Malaise
entities.description: Overwhelming generalized systemic asthenia and physical exhaustion that rapidly bedrides patients within 24 to 48 hours.

entities.name: Severe Lumbosacral Backache
entities.description: Excruciating muscular and spinal discomfort localized to the lumbosacral region, characteristic of early CCHF and Yellow fever.

entities.name: Intractable Watery Diarrhea
entities.description: Massive profuse watery non-bloody diarrhea emerging between days 3 and 5, triggering catastrophic volume depletion.

entities.name: Projectile Vomiting
entities.description: Persistent severe nausea and emesis starting in the early gastrointestinal phase that exacerbates fluid and electrolyte depletion.

entities.name: Severe Epigastric Pain
entities.description: Intense sharp epigastric and periumbilical cramping secondary to viral mucosal inflammation, ischemic enteritis, and pancreatitis.

entities.name: Acute Abdomen Mimicry
entities.description: Severe pseudo-surgical abdominal peritonism and guarding that frequently precipitates hazardous exploratory laparotomies.

entities.name: Diffuse Vascular Hyperpermeability
entities.description: Systemic endothelial barrier breakdown triggered by viral glycoprotein binding and inflammatory cytokine storm.

entities.name: Systemic Capillary Leak
entities.description: Catastrophic plasma fluid extravasation into interstitial spaces and serous cavities causing severe intravascular hypovolemia.

entities.name: Hypovolemic Shock
entities.description: Severe circulatory collapse caused by combining unmitigated gastrointestinal fluid losses with systemic microvascular plasma extravasation.

entities.name: Distributive Vasodilatory Shock
entities.description: Refractory arterial hypotension and loss of vasomotor tone driven by nitric oxide and excessive inflammatory cytokine storm.

entities.name: Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation
entities.description: Systemic consumptive coagulopathy characterized by microvascular thrombi followed by massive bleeding diathesis.

entities.name: Overt Hemorrhagic Diathesis
entities.description: Generalized spontaneous external and internal hemorrhage occurring from multiple mucosal surfaces and skin.

entities.name: Profuse Epistaxis
entities.description: Spontaneous persistent anterior and posterior nasal mucosal hemorrhage that is difficult to arrest.

entities.name: Spontaneous Gingival Bleeding
entities.description: Persistent unprovoked capillary oozing from gums and oral mucosal margins during oral examination.

entities.name: Massive Hematemesis
entities.description: Vomiting of fresh blood or altered coffee-ground material ('black vomit') secondary to erosive gastroduodenal mucosal hemorrhage.

entities.name: Melena and Hematochezia
entities.description: Passage of black tarry stools or frank bright red blood per rectum secondary to extensive lower and upper gastrointestinal hemorrhage.

entities.name: Gross Hematuria
entities.description: Macroscopic blood in the urine caused by extensive renal parenchymal petechiae and glomerular microthrombosis.

entities.name: Severe Menometrorrhagia
entities.description: Abnormal profuse vaginal and uterine bleeding in non-pregnant or pregnant females reflecting severe systemic coagulopathy.

entities.name: Exudative Pharyngitis
entities.description: Severe erythematous tonsillopharyngitis with yellowish-white tonsillar exudates, typical of early Lassa fever.

entities.name: Retrosternal Chest Pain
entities.description: Deep persistent central retrosternal discomfort caused by viral mediastinal lymphadenitis and subepicardial myopericardial inflammation.

entities.name: Acute Hepatocellular Necrosis
entities.description: Extensive destruction of hepatocytes and Councilman body formation leading to acute liver failure.

entities.name: Acute Tubular Necrosis
entities.description: Severe acute kidney injury with oliguria or anuria resulting from profound renal ischemia and direct viral cytopathic effects.

entities.name: Acute Pancreatitis
entities.description: Necroinflammatory injury of the pancreatic parenchyma manifested by intense epigastric distress and hyperamylasemia.

entities.name: Toxic Encephalopathy
entities.description: Acute neuropsychiatric deterioration featuring aggressive delirium, profound confusion, somnolence, and obtundation.

entities.name: Generalized Seizures
entities.description: Tonic-clonic seizures and status epilepticus triggered by severe intracranial hemorrhages, hypoxia, and metabolic acidosis.

entities.name: Sensorineural Hearing Loss
entities.description: Unilateral or bilateral eighth cranial nerve deficit developing in approximately one-third of Lassa fever survivors.

entities.name: Acute Orchitis
entities.description: Severe unilateral or bilateral testicular inflammation, pain, and swelling developing during late disease or convalescence.

entities.name: Severe Uveitis
entities.description: Sight-threatening intraocular inflammation and anterior chamber hypopyon occurring during convalescence from filovirus infection.

entities.name: Spontaneous Abortion
entities.description: Near-universal intrauterine fetal demise and preterm delivery in infected pregnant females accompanied by maternal hemorrhage.

entities.name: Multiorgan Failure Syndrome
entities.description: Simultaneous decompensation of pulmonary, renal, cardiovascular, and hepatic organ systems heralding terminal shock.

entities.name: Severe Pulmonary Edema
entities.description: Non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema with alveolar flooding and acute respiratory distress syndrome.

entities.name: Paralytic Ileus
entities.description: Atonic bowel distension and absence of bowel sounds resulting from diffuse retroperitoneal and visceral autonomic inflammation.

entities.name: Myopericarditis
entities.description: Direct viral inflammation of cardiac myocytes and pericardial lining causing dysrhythmias and pump dysfunction.

entities.name: Splenic Infarction
entities.description: Extensive necrosis and microvascular fibrin thrombosis within splenic red and white pulp.

entities.name: Reactive Hemophagocytosis
entities.description: Hyperactivation of macrophages phagocytosing red blood cells and platelets in bone marrow under massive cytokine stimulation.

entities.name: Facial Periorbital Edema
entities.description: Prominent soft-tissue puffiness and swelling of periorbital tissues, face, and neck reflecting microvascular hyperpermeability.

entities.name: Severe Retro-Orbital Pain
entities.description: Deep aching retrobulbar cephalalgia exacerbated by extraocular movements during early viraemic prodrome.

entities.name: Extensive Cutaneous Desquamation
entities.description: Widespread fine branny or sheet-like exfoliation of skin over the palms, soles, and trunk during convalescence.

entities.name: Post-Viral Arthralgia Syndrome
entities.description: Persistent severe joint pain, fatigue, and muscular aches continuing for months or years in VHF survivors.

entities.name: Faget Sign
entities.description: Sphygmothermic dissociation characterized by high fever paired with paradoxical relative bradycardia, classic for Yellow fever.

entities.name: Ghost-Like Sunken Eyes
entities.description: Striking enophthalmos paired with a blank, mask-like, impassive expression reflecting profound dehydration and exhaustion.

entities.name: Venipuncture Site Bleeding
entities.description: Incessant, uncontrolled bloody weeping and expanding subcutaneous hematomas around intravenous cannula and blood-draw punctures.

entities.name: Palatal Petechial Enanthem
entities.description: Clusters of discrete pinpoint purpuric mucosal hemorrhages scattered across the soft palate and uvula.

entities.name: Subconjunctival Hemorrhage
entities.description: Extensive bright red extravasation of blood under the bulbar conjunctiva creating sheet-like scleral hematomas.

entities.name: Non-Purulent Conjunctival Injection
entities.description: Intense bilateral bulbar and palpebral ciliary flush without mucopurulent discharge in early disease.

entities.name: Morbilliform Maculopapular Rash
entities.description: Non-pruritic erythematous, maculopapular eruption developing on trunk, neck, and arms around days 5 to 7.

entities.name: Severe Facial Flushing
entities.description: Intense confluent dusky erythema covering the face, neck, and upper thorax during early viremia.

entities.name: Petechial Skin Eruption
entities.description: Multiple pinpoint non-blanching violaceous petechiae coalescing over dependent areas and pressure points.

entities.name: Large Cutaneous Ecchymoses
entities.description: Spontaneous confluent blue-black subcutaneous extravasations spreading rapidly across the extremities and trunk.

entities.name: Delayed Capillary Refill
entities.description: Prolongation of distal capillary bed blanch recovery beyond 3 to 4 seconds indicating severe peripheral hypoperfusion.

entities.name: Mask-Like Blank Facies
entities.description: Fixed, unblinking, expressionless facial appearance resulting from severe encephalopathy and neurovascular exhaustion.

entities.name: Tender Hepatomegaly
entities.description: Smooth, exquisitely tender enlargement of the liver edge 2 to 4 cm below the right costal margin.

entities.name: Palpable Splenomegaly
entities.description: Soft, palpable splenic enlargement extending below the left costal margin in 15% to 35% of patients.

entities.name: Cervical Lymphadenopathy
entities.description: Tender bilateral anterior and posterior cervical lymph node enlargement accompanying pharyngeal inflammation.

entities.name: Deep Jaundice
entities.description: Intense yellow-orange discoloration of the sclerae and skin appearing rapidly during the toxic stage of Yellow fever.

entities.name: Extreme Postural Hypotension
entities.description: Severe drop in systolic blood pressure (>20-30 mmHg) upon standing, progressing to persistent supine hypotension.

entities.name: Asterixis and Tremor
entities.description: Flapping tremor of dorsiflexed hands and coarse resting tremor reflecting severe hepatic and metabolic encephalopathy.

entities.name: Cold Clammy Extremities
entities.description: Mottled, cool, and diaphoretic distal limbs reflecting profound intense compensatory vasoconstriction.

entities.name: Spontaneous Gingival Oozing
entities.description: Persistent unprovoked microvascular bleeding and hematoma formation along dental arches.

entities.name: Marked Lumbosacral Tenderness
entities.description: Severe localized tenderness upon palpation of the lower spine and paraspinal muscles.

entities.name: Agitated Delirium
entities.description: Severe motor restlessness, combative agitation, and acute confusion occurring in toxic encephalopathy.

entities.name: Coma and Unresponsiveness
entities.description: Profound unarousable coma with loss of protective airway reflexes in terminal multi-organ collapse.

entities.name: Severe Tachypnea
entities.description: Rapid, shallow respiratory rate exceeding 30 breaths per minute compensating for profound metabolic lactic acidosis.

entities.name: Unilateral Scrotal Swelling
entities.description: Acute marked enlargement, erythema, and exquisite tenderness of the testicle and hemiscrotum in convalescing males.

entities.name: Hypothermia During Shock
entities.description: Paradoxical plunge of core body temperature below 36°C preceding terminal cardiovascular arrest.

entities.name: Involuntary Muscular Fasciculations
entities.description: Fine rapid twitching of perioral and limb muscle groups reflecting central neurotoxic irritation.

entities.name: Profound Thrombocytopenia
entities.description: Rapid steep drop in circulating platelets below 50,000/uL and frequently < 20,000/uL within 3 to 5 days.

entities.name: Biphasic Leukocyte Count
entities.description: Initial severe leukopenia (WBC < 3,000/uL) rapidly reversing during shock to leukocytosis with immature myeloid forms.

entities.name: Severe Early Lymphopenia
entities.description: Massive destruction and apoptotic loss of peripheral circulating lymphocytes during the early viraemic phase.

entities.name: Massive Transaminitis
entities.description: Serum transaminase elevations into the thousands (1,000 to 10,000+ U/L) indicating widespread hepatocyte and tissue lysis.

entities.name: High AST ALT Ratio
entities.description: Disproportionate elevation of AST compared to ALT exceeding 3:1 to 5:1, reflecting diffuse hepatocellular, myocardial, and lymphoid necrosis.

entities.name: Markedly Prolonged PT
entities.description: Prolongation of prothrombin time and INR > 1.5-2.0 indicating failure of extrinsic pathway and factor VII depletion.

entities.name: Significantly Prolonged aPTT
entities.description: Prolongation of activated partial thromboplastin time exceeding 60 seconds, a primary Swanepoel predictor of fatal outcome.

entities.name: Severe Hypofibrinogenemia
entities.description: Precipitous drop of plasma fibrinogen below 100-110 mg/dL reflecting unmitigated consumption in microthrombi.

entities.name: Elevated Fibrin Degradation Products
entities.description: Massive accumulation of circulating FDPs from widespread plasmin degradation of crosslinked fibrin.

entities.name: Massively Elevated D-Dimer
entities.description: High quantitative D-dimer levels indicating ongoing active fibrin deposition and breakdown in microvessels.

entities.name: Markedly Elevated Ferritin
entities.description: Extreme serum ferritin elevations exceeding 5,000 to 10,000 ng/mL driven by severe macrophage activation.

entities.name: Severe Lactic Acidosis
entities.description: High arterial blood lactate (>4 to 8 mmol/L) with severe wide anion-gap metabolic acidosis indicating anaerobic metabolism.

entities.name: Elevated Serum Creatinine
entities.description: Progressive doubling of serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen heralding acute tubular necrosis.

entities.name: Elevated Creatine Kinase
entities.description: Marked elevation of serum CK (>1,000 to 5,000 U/L) resulting from viral myositis and ischemic muscle necrosis.

entities.name: Elevated Lactate Dehydrogenase
entities.description: Extremely high serum LDH (>1,000 U/L) reflecting extensive widespread tissue breakdown and cell lysis.

entities.name: Serum Amylase Elevation
entities.description: Marked elevations of circulating pancreatic enzymes reflecting acute viral injury and ischemia of the pancreas.

entities.name: Severe Hyponatremia
entities.description: Serum sodium dropping below 130 mEq/L resulting from profuse diarrhea, vomiting, and non-osmotic ADH release.

entities.name: Severe Hypokalemia
entities.description: Precipitous fall of serum potassium below 3.0 mEq/L driven by uncompensated gastrointestinal losses.

entities.name: Terminal Hyperkalemia
entities.description: Fatal surge of potassium exceeding 6.5 mEq/L caused by acute anuric renal failure and massive cell lysis.

entities.name: Severe Hypocalcemia
entities.description: Depression of ionized serum calcium caused by saponification in peripancreatic fat and severe hypoalbuminemia.

entities.name: Hypoalbuminemia
entities.description: Serum albumin falling below 2.0-2.5 g/dL resulting from capillary leakage into third spaces.

entities.name: Positive RT-PCR Assay
entities.description: Molecular identification of viral RNA genomes in blood samples confirming acute viral replication.

entities.name: High Viremia RNA Copy
entities.description: Extremely high viral copy numbers (Ct < 20 or > 10^7 copies/mL) strongly correlating with fatal outcome.

entities.name: Positive Antigen Capture ELISA
entities.description: Enzymatic detection of circulating viral nucleoprotein or glycoprotein in acute-phase blood.

entities.name: Specific IgM Seropositivity
entities.description: Demonstration of anti-viral IgM antibodies by capture ELISA from day 7 post-onset.

entities.name: Viral Isolation BSL-4
entities.description: Propagation of live infectious virus from blood onto Vero or LLC-MK2 cell cultures under maximum biocontainment.

entities.name: Absent Neutralizing Antibodies
entities.description: Complete failure to develop specific neutralizing IgG antibodies during the second week of illness in fatal cases.

entities.name: Elevated Inflammatory Cytokines
entities.description: Dramatic elevation of plasma TNF-alpha, IL-6, IL-1beta, and IFN-gamma with depressed IL-10.

entities.name: Microscopic Hematuria
entities.description: Urinalysis revealing numerous dysmorphic erythrocytes, cellular casts, and gross proteinuria.

entities.name: B-Lines on Lung Ultrasound
entities.description: Point-of-care lung ultrasonography demonstrating multiple confluent vertical reverberation artifacts.

entities.name: Gallbladder Wall Thickening
entities.description: Sonographic demonstration of edematous striation and thickening of the gallbladder wall (>3 mm) without stones.

entities.name: Bilateral Pleural Effusions
entities.description: Anechoic fluid accumulations in both costophrenic angles on chest ultrasound or radiography.

entities.name: Ascites on Ultrasound
entities.description: Free peritoneal fluid visualized in the hepatorenal space, spleno-renal angle, and pelvis on bedside POCUS.

entities.name: Pericardial Effusion on Echo
entities.description: Hypoechoic fluid separation between the visceral and parietal pericardium on focused cardiac ultrasound.

entities.name: Fluid-Filled Bowel Loops
entities.description: Distended, aperistaltic intestinal loops filled with static intraluminal fluid on abdominal ultrasonography.

entities.name: Diffuse Hepatic Steatosis
entities.description: Marked increased hepatic echogenicity and sound attenuation on liver ultrasonography.

entities.name: Splenomegaly on Ultrasound
entities.description: Bipolar measurement of the spleen exceeding 13 cm with prominent splenic vein engorgement.

entities.name: Bilateral Interstitial Infiltrates
entities.description: Diffuse symmetrical perihilar ground-glass haziness on chest radiography indicating capillary alveolar leakage.

entities.name: Infected Patient Body Fluids
entities.description: Direct cutaneous or mucosal contact with blood, vomitus, diarrhea, saliva, or sweat of symptomatic VHF patients.

entities.name: Unsafe Burial Practices
entities.description: Traditional mourning rituals involving direct touching, washing, and preparing deceased VHF corpses harboring peak viral titers.

entities.name: Percutaneous Needlestick Injury
entities.description: Accidental inoculation with hollow-bore contaminated needles during patient care or phlebotomy.

entities.name: Contaminated Medical Equipment
entities.description: Reuse or unsterilized handling of syringes, surgical scalpels, and intravenous tubing across healthcare facilities.

entities.name: Rousettus aegyptiacus Fruit Bats
entities.description: Egyptian fruit bats inhabiting caves and abandoned mines, representing the natural reservoir host of Marburg virus.

entities.name: Mastomys natalensis Excreta
entities.description: Urine, feces, and saliva of the multimammate rat contaminating domestic food and household dust in West Africa.

entities.name: Hyalomma Marginatum Tick Bite
entities.description: Bites of Hyalomma marginatum marginatum ticks in scrublands, pastures, and agricultural fields of Eurasia and Africa.

entities.name: Crushing Engorged Ticks
entities.description: Crushing ticks with bare fingers while grooming livestock, causing direct percutaneous viral inoculation.

entities.name: Viraemic Livestock Blood
entities.description: Contact with fresh blood, tissues, and viscera of infected cattle, sheep, goats, or ostriches during butchering.

entities.name: Aedes Mosquito Bite
entities.description: Bites of diurnal anthropophilic Aedes aegypti mosquitoes in urban and peri-domestic environments.

entities.name: Haemagogus Mosquito Bite
entities.description: Bites of canopy-dwelling Haemagogus mosquitoes in South American tropical rainforests.

entities.name: Contaminated Semen Exposure
entities.description: Unprotected sexual contact with convalescent male survivors shedding persistent virus from immune-privileged testes.

entities.name: Non-Human Primate Contact
entities.description: Hunting, butchering, or handling dead or moribund chimpanzees, gorillas, or monkeys in rainforests.

entities.name: Frontline Healthcare Workers
entities.description: Physicians, nurses, phlebotomists, and hospital cleaners delivering acute care without adequate barrier PPE.

entities.name: Slaughterhouse Workers
entities.description: Abattoir personnel, butchers, and meat dressers eviscerating livestock in CCHF-endemic pastoral zones.

entities.name: Subsistence Pastoral Farmers
entities.description: Rural farmers, agricultural workers, and livestock handlers living in Hyalomma tick habitats.

entities.name: Subterranean Mine Workers
entities.description: Miners working in poorly ventilated subterranean gold or cobalt shafts harboring large bat colonies.

entities.name: Pregnant Women
entities.description: Expectant mothers undergoing profound immunological alterations with massive viral tropism for the placenta.

entities.name: Laboratory Personnel BSL-4
entities.description: Microbiologists and clinical pathologists handling un-inactivated specimens without full BSL-4 containment.

entities.name: Incubation Two to Twenty-One
entities.description: Standard incubation period for Ebola and Marburg viruses typically extending from 2 to 21 days (mean 5 to 10 days).

entities.name: Incubation Period 1-9 Days
entities.description: Rapid incubation window for CCHF following an infected Hyalomma tick bite, averaging 1 to 3 days.

entities.name: Incubation Period 6-21 Days
entities.description: Insidious incubation interval for Lassa fever following rodent excreta ingestion or mucosal contact.

entities.name: Incubation Period 3-6 Days
entities.description: Short acute incubation period for Yellow fever following the infective bite of an Aedes or Haemagogus mosquito.

entities.name: Absence of Endemic Travel
entities.description: Absence of travel to or contact with endemic areas within 21 days definitively excludes acute VHF.

entities.name: Chronic Symptoms Over Month
entities.description: Continuous symptoms lasting >3 to 4 weeks prior to presentation is incompatible with acute VHF.

entities.name: Normal Platelet Count
entities.description: Completely normal platelet count (>150,000/uL) during acute severe illness rules out acute VHF.

entities.name: Isolated Marked Thrombocytosis
entities.description: Elevated platelets (>450,000/uL) reflects a reactive or non-VHF process, excluding viral coagulopathy.

entities.name: Normal Coagulation Parameters
entities.description: Entirely normal PT/INR, aPTT, and fibrinogen in a severely toxic febrile patient excludes acute VHF.

entities.name: Prompt Antibiotic Response
entities.description: Rapid defervescence and stabilization within 24 to 48 hours of antibacterial therapy excludes VHF.

entities.name: High Procalcitonin Level
entities.description: Serum procalcitonin >10 ng/mL strongly indicates severe pyogenic bacterial sepsis rather than uncomplicated VHF.

entities.name: Positive Thick Blood Smear
entities.description: Identification of asexual Plasmodium falciparum parasites establishes malaria as the primary etiology.

entities.name: Focal Lobar Consolidation
entities.description: Dense unilateral lobar airspace consolidation on imaging indicates primary bacterial pneumonia.

entities.name: Preserved Lymphocyte Count
entities.description: Normal or elevated absolute lymphocyte counts during early toxic fever contradicts typical VHF lymphopenia.

entities.name: Absence of Transaminitis
entities.description: Completely normal serum AST and ALT in an acutely deteriorating patient rules out hepatotropic VHF.

entities.name: Normal Serum Ferritin
entities.description: Normal ferritin (<300 ng/mL) contradicts the profound hyperferritinemic cytokine storm characteristic of VHF.

entities.name: Profuse Pruritic Urticaria
entities.description: Intensely itchy hives or wheals indicate allergic or parasitic etiology, unlike the non-itchy VHF rash.

entities.name: Purulent Conjunctival Discharge
entities.description: Copious yellow-green purulent ocular exudate and crusting indicates pyogenic bacterial conjunctivitis.

entities.name: Isolated Leukocytosis Day One
entities.description: Massive neutrophilia (>15,000/uL) on fever day 1 without preceding leukopenia indicates bacterial infection.

entities.name: Chronic Firm Splenomegaly
entities.description: Hard, massive splenomegaly persisting for months indicates chronic visceral leishmaniasis, malaria, or cirrhosis.

entities.name: Positive Bacterial Blood Culture
entities.description: Growth of pyogenic pathogens (e.g., Neisseria meningitidis, Salmonella) demonstrates primary bacterial bacteremia.

entities.name: Negative RT-PCR Day Four
entities.description: A negative RT-PCR assay performed on blood collected on or after day 4 of symptoms excludes VHF viremia.

entities.name: Normal Blood Lactate
entities.description: Normal blood lactate (<1.5 mmol/L) in a patient presenting with shock contradicts microcirculatory collapse of VHF.

entities.name: Isolated Hematuria Normal Platelets
entities.description: Hematuria with normal platelet count and intact clotting screens points to local urinary pathology rather than VHF.

entities.name: Normal Gallbladder Wall Thickness
entities.description: Sonographically thin, normal gallbladder wall (<2 mm) without pericholecystic edema argues against VHF capillary leak.

entities.name: Immediate Antimalarial Response
entities.description: Prompt fever resolution and clinical recovery within 24-48 hours of artemisinin or chloroquine confirms malaria.

entities.name: Severe Dengue
entities.description: Severe mosquito-borne flaviviral infection characterized by critical capillary leak timed strictly to defervescence (days 3-7).

entities.name: Falciparum Malaria
entities.description: Protozoan parasitemia causing cyclical high fever, intraerythrocytic schizogony, hemolytic anemia, and rapid response to artesunate.

entities.name: Leptospirosis
entities.description: Zoonotic spirochetal infection presenting with marked conjunctival suffusion, severe calf tenderness, day-1 neutrophilia, and penicillin responsiveness.

entities.name: Typhoid Fever
entities.description: Systemic enteric fever caused by Salmonella Typhi presenting with step-ladder fever, rose spots, and bacteremia.

entities.name: Meningococcemia
entities.description: Fulminant Neisseria meningitidis bacteremia causing explosive purpura fulminans, rapid shock, and neutrophilic CSF pleocytosis.

entities.name: Acute Bacterial Sepsis
entities.description: Life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by dysregulated host response to localized pyogenic bacterial infection.

entities.name: Rickettsial Disease
entities.description: Tick- or flea-borne intracellular bacterial infection causing fever, characteristic inoculation eschar, centripetal rash, and doxycycline cure.

entities.name: Acute Viral Hepatitis
entities.description: Acute hepatotropic viral infection (HAV, HBV, HEV) featuring profound ALT-predominant transaminitis without early DIC or shock.

entities.name: Shigellosis
entities.description: Acute bacterial invasive enterocolitis causing inflammatory dysentery, tenesmus, and high fecal leukocytes.

entities.name: Acute Appendicitis
entities.description: Focal bacterial inflammation of the vermiform appendix presenting with localized McBurney point tenderness and intact platelets.

entities.name: Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura
entities.description: Microangiopathic hemolytic anemia driven by ADAMTS13 deficiency with abundant schistocytes and normal clotting times.

entities.name: Immune Thrombocytopenic Purpura
entities.description: Isolated autoimmune platelet destruction with normal liver function, normal coagulation parameters, and no systemic toxic fever.

entities.name: Yellow Fever
entities.description: Endemic flaviviral hemorrhagic fever characterized by Faget sign, midzonal hepatic Councilman bodies, and prevention by 17D vaccine.

entities.name: Lassa Fever
entities.description: Arenaviral hemorrhagic fever endemic to West Africa featuring exudative pharyngitis, retrosternal chest pain, sensorineural deafness, and ribavirin sensitivity.

entities.name: Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever
entities.description: Nairoviral tick-borne infection transmitted by Hyalomma ticks presenting with severe lumbosacral pain, agricultural exposure, and ribavirin sensitivity.

entities.name: Marburg Virus Disease
entities.description: Filoviral hemorrhagic fever linked to Rousettus bat caves with up to 88% case fatality and complete insensitivity to ribavirin.

entities.name: Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome
entities.description: Bunyaviral respiratory infection caused by Sin Nombre virus presenting with non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema without prominent bleeding diathesis.

entities.name: Plague
entities.description: Yersinia pestis zoonosis presenting with suppurative regional buboes, safety-pin bacilli on Gram stain, and response to streptomycin.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, sudden fever onset, high continuous fever, rigors, acute viraemia
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Sudden dramatic onset of high continuous fever (>39°C) with rigors and prostrating chills marking the acute viremic phase of viral hemorrhagic fevers.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, severe asthenia, profound weakness, bedridden, rapid prostration
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Overwhelming systemic asthenia and severe debilitating weakness that rapidly incapacitates patients within 24 to 48 hours of onset.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, lumbar pain, backache, musculoskeletal pain, CCHF prodrome
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Excruciating musculoskeletal pain localized to the lumbar spine and lower back, a classical early prodromal feature of CCHF and Yellow fever.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, profuse diarrhea, watery stools, volume loss, filovirus gastrointestinal
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Massive copious non-bloody watery diarrhea emerging around days 3 to 5 in Ebola and Marburg, causing rapid severe hypovolemic dehydration.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, severe vomiting, emesis, electrolyte depletion, gastrointestinal phase
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Frequent unrelenting nausea and emesis beginning in the early gastrointestinal phase, accelerating fluid and electrolyte depletion.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, epigastric tenderness, abdominal cramping, mucosal ischemia, enteritis
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Sharp intense epigastric and diffuse abdominal cramping secondary to mucosal ischemia, viral pancreatitis, and visceral congestion.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, pseudo-surgical abdomen, peritonism, misdiagnosis, surgical hazard
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Pseudo-surgical peritonitis and severe rebound-like abdominal tenderness that frequently leads to hazardous emergency surgical interventions in undiagnosed VHF.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, endothelial barrier breakdown, capillary permeability, third spacing
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Widespread systemic capillary leak syndrome driven by viral glycoprotein-induced endothelial activation, shedding, and barrier breakdown.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, plasma extravasation, third-spacing, serous cavities, hypovolemia
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Massive third-spacing of fluid into serous cavities and interstitial spaces leading to critical intravascular hypovolemia.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, circulatory failure, hypovolemia, dehydration, vascular collapse
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Rapid cardiovascular collapse from severe intravascular volume depletion driven by combined gastrointestinal fluid losses and microvascular plasma extravasation.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, vasodilatory shock, cytokine storm, nitric oxide, hypotension
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Refractory hypotension resulting from severe cytokine storm (TNF-alpha, IL-6, IL-1), endothelial nitric oxide release, and loss of vasomotor tone.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, consumptive coagulopathy, microvascular thrombosis, DIC, coagulation failure
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Widespread microvascular thrombosis paired with catastrophic consumption of platelets and clotting factors causing multiorgan ischemia and systemic bleeding.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, bleeding diathesis, mucosal bleeding, internal hemorrhage, toxic phase
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Uncontrolled generalized bleeding diathesis emerging around days 5 to 7 due to combined severe thrombocytopenia and consumptive coagulopathy.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, epistaxis, nosebleed, nasal mucosal bleeding, coagulopathy
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Severe spontaneous anterior and posterior nasal mucosal bleeding that is difficult to tamponade in advanced coagulopathy.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, gingival hemorrhage, gum bleeding, oral mucosa, coagulopathy
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Continuous unprovoked hemorrhage and oozing from gingival margins and oral mucous membranes.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, hematemesis, black vomit, upper GI bleeding, gastric erosions
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Severe vomiting of fresh blood or altered 'black vomit' caused by diffuse gastric mucosal ulcerations and severe coagulopathy.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, melena, hematochezia, lower GI bleed, rectal hemorrhage
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Evacuation of altered black tarry stools or frank rectal bleeding reflecting extensive mucosal hemorrhage throughout the digestive tract.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, hematuria, macroscopic renal bleed, urinary tract hemorrhage
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Macroscopic renal bleeding and red-tinged urine secondary to glomerular microthrombosis and renal parenchymal hemorrhage.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, menometrorrhagia, uterine hemorrhage, vaginal bleeding, coagulopathy
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Profuse spontaneous uterine and vaginal hemorrhage in females, often triggering spontaneous abortion in pregnant patients.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, tonsillopharyngitis, exudative sore throat, dysphagia, Lassa hallmark
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Painful erythematous pharyngitis and tonsillitis often accompanied by white exudates and severe dysphagia, particularly prominent in Lassa fever.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, retrosternal pain, chest discomfort, pericardial inflammation, Lassa fever
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Intense retrosternal thoracic discomfort and pericardial-like chest pain caused by viral myopericarditis and mediastinal lymphatic involvement in Lassa fever.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, liver failure, Councilman bodies, hepatocyte lysis, Yellow fever
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Extensive midzonal or focal hepatic necrosis triggered by direct viral cytolysis in Kupffer cells and hepatocytes, especially prominent in Yellow fever.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, acute kidney injury, oliguria, anuria, tubular ischemia
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Severe oliguric or anuric renal failure resulting from a combination of renal hypoperfusion, microvascular thrombosis, and viral nephrotoxicity.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, pancreatic necrosis, hyperamylasemia, epigastric pain, viral injury
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Severe epigastric necrosis and marked pancreatic enzyme elevation resulting from viral parenchymal infiltration and microischemia.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, delirium, agitation, confusion, cerebral edema, toxic encephalopathy
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Profound neurocognitive dysfunction characterized by severe delirium, extreme irritability, belligerent confusion, obtundation, and coma.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, convulsions, status epilepticus, intracranial hemorrhage, metabolic coma
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Terminal convulsive status or focal motor seizures precipitated by cerebral hypoperfusion, intracranial petechial bleeding, and metabolic collapse.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, deafness, eighth nerve palsy, auditory loss, Lassa sequela
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Acute early or delayed cranial nerve VIII eighth-nerve deafness occurring in up to one-third of Lassa fever patients, often permanent.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, orchitis, testicular pain, scrotal swelling, immune privileged persistence
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Painful unilateral or bilateral testicular inflammation occurring during the late phase or convalescence due to viral persistence in immune-privileged scrotal tissues.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, ocular inflammation, uveitis, vision loss, convalescent filovirus
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Intense anterior or posterior ocular inflammation and photophobia arising during late or convalescent disease due to filoviral ocular persistence.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, miscarriage, fetal demise, pregnancy complication, placental infection
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Near-universal fetal loss, severe maternal hemorrhage, and high fetal/maternal mortality during pregnancy due to tropism for placental syncytiotrophoblasts.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, multiple organ dysfunction, systemic collapse, refractory shock, death
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Combined decompensation of renal, hepatic, respiratory, and cardiovascular organ systems leading to refractory cardiopulmonary arrest.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, pulmonary edema, ARDS, respiratory distress, capillary leak
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Acute non-cardiogenic alveolar fluid flooding and respiratory failure secondary to diffuse endothelial barrier destruction and capillary leak.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, intestinal atony, absent bowel sounds, abdominal distension, ileus
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Severe intestinal adynamia and abdominal distension caused by visceral autonomic inflammation, mucosal edema, and electrolyte depletion.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, cardiac dysfunction, pericardial rub, myocarditis, arrhythmia
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Direct viral replication in cardiomyocytes and pericardial lining causing arrhythmia, pericardial rub, and poor cardiac contractility.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, splenic necrosis, white pulp depletion, lymphoid lysis, microthrombosis
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Massive lymphoid depletion and microvascular fibrin thrombi in the white pulp leading to splenic necrosis and impaired immune clearance.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, macrophage activation, hemophagocytosis, bone marrow, cytopenia
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Pathologic macrophage activation and hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) in bone marrow driven by hypercytokinemia, worsening cytopenias.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, periorbital swelling, facial puffiness, capillary leakage, soft tissue edema
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Striking soft tissue swelling of the face, neck, and periorbital spaces caused by regional microvascular permeability and venous congestion.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, retro-orbital headache, ocular pain, extraocular movements, prodrome
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Intense ocular cephalalgia exacerbated by eye movement, reflecting acute microvascular congestion and retro-orbital inflammation.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, skin peeling, epidermal shedding, desquamation, convalescent phase
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Diffuse superficial epidermal peeling and shedding of palms and soles occurring during the late convalescent phase following resolution of the rash.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, chronic joint pain, post-Ebola syndrome, survivor sequelae, myalgia
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Prolonged debilitating polyarthralgias, musculoskeletal fatigue, and recurrent myalgias persisting for months to years in VHF survivors.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, sphygmothermic dissociation, relative bradycardia, Yellow fever hallmark
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Sphygmothermic dissociation where severe high fever is accompanied by profound, paradoxical relative bradycardia, pathognomonic of the toxic phase of Yellow fever.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, enophthalmos, sunken eyes, facies cholerica, expressionless face, filovirus
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Deeply recessed enophthalmos paired with an expressionless, blank, mask-like facies ('facies cholerica') reflecting catastrophic dehydration and extreme toxic exhaustion in Ebola and Marburg.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, catheter site oozing, needle puncture bleeding, consumptive coagulopathy
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Persistent, uncontrollable uncoagulated bloody weeping and expanding hematomas at all peripheral intravenous catheter and blood draw sites, pathognomonic of fulminant consumption coagulopathy.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, soft palate petechiae, enanthem, uvula purpura, CCHF early sign
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Pinpoint purpuric petechial spots across the soft palate and uvula appearing prior to cutaneous petechiae, classic for early CCHF and Arenavirus infection.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, scleral bleeding, red eyes, subconjunctival suffusion, hemorrhagic sign
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Dramatic bright red scleral suffusion and flame-shaped subconjunctival extravasation occurring bilaterally without ocular discharge.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, ciliary flush, glassy eyes, non-purulent injection, early prodrome
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Prominent bilateral ciliary flush and glassy conjunctival hyperemia in the early prodromal phase distinguishing VHF from bacterial conjunctivitis.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, maculopapular rash, morbilliform eruption, trunk rash, filovirus rash
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Non-pruritic erythematous, maculopapular eruption developing on the trunk, neck, and arms between days 5 and 7, classic for filovirus infections.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, facial erythema, neck flushing, sun-burnt appearance, early viremia
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Intense diffuse erythema and hyperaemia covering the face, neck, and upper chest during the early prehemorrhagic viremic stage.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, petechiae, non-blanching spots, purpuric rash, microvascular bleeding
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Widespread pinpoint non-blanching violaceous petechiae coalescing into extensive purpura over pressure points, torso, and extremities.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, ecchymoses, subcutaneous hematomas, skin bruising, hemorrhagic diathesis
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Spontaneous extensive subcutaneous hematomas and confluent sheet-like purpuric lesions across extremities and trunk.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, capillary refill >3s, poor peripheral perfusion, cold extremities, shock
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Prolonged capillary refill time (>3 to 4 seconds) in cold, clammy distal extremities indicating profound peripheral vasoconstriction and hypovolemia.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, hypomimia, impassive face, blank stare, severe exhaustion
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Hypomimic, impassive facial appearance resulting from profound neurovascular exhaustion, extreme weakness, and encephalopathy.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, hepatic enlargement, right upper quadrant tenderness, acute hepatitis
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Smooth, exquisitely tender enlargement of the liver extending 2 to 4 cm below the right costal margin reflecting acute hepatic inflammation and distension.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, splenic enlargement, splenomegaly, reticuloendothelial congestion
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Moderate splenomegaly detected in 15% to 35% of CCHF and Lassa fever cases reflecting acute reticuloendothelial congestion.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, lymphadenopathy, neck nodes, tender lymph nodes, Lassa fever sign
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Tender anterior and posterior cervical lymphadenopathy accompanying severe exudative pharyngitis in Lassa fever.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, icterus, scleral icterus, yellow skin, acute hepatic failure
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Marked icteric discoloration of sclerae and skin appearing rapidly during the toxic phase of Yellow fever and advanced filoviral hepatic necrosis.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, orthostatic drop, low blood pressure, severe hypovolemia, shock state
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Severe orthostatic blood pressure drops and resting profound hypotension (systolic BP < 80 mmHg) indicative of imminent cardiovascular collapse.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, flapping tremor, hepatic encephalopathy, motor instability, asterixis
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Flapping tremor of extended hands and coarse intention tremor reflecting acute hepatic encephalopathy and metabolic derangement.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, mottling, cool limbs, clammy skin, peripheral vasoconstriction, shock
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Peripheral cyanosis, hypothermia, and cool mottled skin over hands and feet heralding decompensated circulatory shock.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, gum bleeding, oral oozing, hemorrhagic sign, mucosal fragility
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Continuous slow capillary oozing of blood from spongy, swollen gums upon light inspection or tongue depression.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, spinal tenderness, lumbar palpation, paraspinal spasm, CCHF sign
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Severe paraspinal and spinal tenderness upon light palpation of the lower lumbar vertebrae, typical of early CCHF.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, motor agitation, delirium, combative state, cerebral irritation
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Severe motor restlessness, disorientation, combative behavior, and confusion indicative of cerebral edema and toxic encephalopathy.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, unarousable state, deep coma, Glasgow Coma Scale drop, terminal failure
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Rapid deterioration from somnolence to profound unarousable coma in the late stages of multiorgan collapse.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, tachypnea, rapid breathing, Kussmaul respiration, metabolic acidosis
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Rapid shallow respiration (>30 breaths/min) driven by compensatory response to profound metabolic lactic acidosis and non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, scrotal enlargement, testicular tenderness, orchitis, convalescent sign
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Acute tender enlargement, warmth, and erythema of the hemiscrotum indicating virus-induced orchitis in convalescent males.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, hypothermia, low body temp, terminal shock, cardiovascular collapse
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Sudden drop of body temperature below 36°C preceding terminal cardiovascular collapse in fulminant filovirus infection.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, muscle twitching, fasciculations, neuromuscular irritation, neurotoxin
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Fine localized twitching and fasciculations of facial and limb muscles indicating central neurovascular irritation.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, low platelets, thrombocytopenia <20000, consumptive coagulopathy
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Precipitous, rapid collapse of platelet count routinely dropping below 50,000/uL and often < 20,000/uL within the first 3 to 5 days of illness.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, early leukopenia, late leukocytosis, left shift, biphasic WBC
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Early marked leukopenia (WBC < 3,000/uL) with lymphopenia, switching rapidly during toxic shock to dramatic neutrophilia with severe left shift.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, absolute lymphopenia, lymphocyte apoptosis, immune depletion
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Catastrophic absolute lymphocyte depletion (< 1,000/uL) caused by massive bystander apoptosis of T and B lymphocytes.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, high AST ALT, liver cytolysis, transaminitis >1000, hepatic necrosis
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Serum aspartate aminotransferase (AST) elevating to 1,000-10,000 U/L, vastly exceeding alanine aminotransferase (ALT) with an AST:ALT ratio > 3:1 to 5:1.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, AST > ALT, AST:ALT ratio >3:1, tissue lysis, diagnostic biomarker
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Markedly skewed ratio of AST to ALT exceeding 3:1 reflecting combined hepatocellular cytolysis, lymphoid breakdown, and diffuse myonecrosis.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, prolonged PT, high INR, extrinsic pathway failure, coagulopathy
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Severe elevation of prothrombin time and international normalized ratio reflecting hepatic synthetic failure and consumptive coagulopathy.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, aPTT >60s, intrinsic pathway, Swanepoel mortality predictor, DIC
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Marked prolongation of activated partial thromboplastin time (> 60 seconds) predicting high mortality under Swanepoel criteria.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, fibrinogen <100 mg/dL, consumptive DIC, factor depletion
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Severe hypofibrinogenemia (< 100 mg/dL) reflecting massive consumption of clotting substrates in widespread microvascular thrombosis.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, FDP elevation, fibrinolysis, consumptive coagulopathy, DIC
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Striking increase in plasma FDP concentrations secondary to uninhibited secondary fibrinolysis in fulminant DIC.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, high D-dimer, crosslinked fibrin, microvascular thrombosis, DIC
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] High quantitative D-dimer levels indicating ongoing diffuse intravascular coagulation and cross-linked fibrin clot breakdown.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, hyperferritinemia >5000, cytokine storm, macrophage activation, HLH
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Extreme hyperferritinemia (> 5,000 to > 10,000 ng/mL) reflecting hypercytokinemia, macrophage activation, and acute cellular necrosis.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, lactic acidosis, high lactate >4, wide anion gap, tissue hypoperfusion
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Profound arterial lactic acidosis (lactate > 4 to 8 mmol/L) and wide anion gap driven by systemic tissue hypoperfusion and anaerobic metabolism.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, renal azotemia, acute kidney injury, high creatinine, BUN rise
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Rapid doubling or tripling of baseline serum creatinine and BUN reflecting acute tubular necrosis and prerenal azotemia.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, high CK, creatine phosphokinase, rhabdomyolysis, myositis
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Striking elevation of CK (often > 1,000-5,000 U/L) indicating diffuse viral rhabdomyolysis and widespread muscle injury.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, high LDH, tissue breakdown, cellular necrosis, cellular turnover
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Marked LDH elevation (> 1,000 U/L) reflecting extensive tissue ischemia, red blood cell lysis, and cellular turnover.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, hyperamylasemia, high lipase, viral pancreatitis, pancreatic injury
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Significant rise in serum amylase and lipase indicating viral pancreatic inflammation and microvascular injury.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, low sodium, hyponatremia <130, SIADH, gastrointestinal loss
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Serum sodium < 130 mEq/L resulting from severe gastrointestinal electrolyte losses, third-spacing, and syndrome of inappropriate ADH.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, low potassium, hypokalemia <3.0, diarrhea loss, arrhythmia risk
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Profound potassium depletion (< 3.0 mEq/L) driven by massive diarrhea and vomiting during the early toxic phase.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, high potassium >6.5, anuria, fatal hyperkalemia, cell lysis
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Fatal serum potassium surge (> 6.5 mEq/L) precipitated by acute anuric renal failure, extensive cell lysis, and acidosis.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, low ionized calcium, hypocalcemia, pancreatitis saponification
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Marked decrease in ionized calcium secondary to acute pancreatitis, free fatty acid saponification, and massive albumin loss.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, low albumin <2.5, capillary leak, third-spacing, hepatic failure
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Precipitous decline in serum albumin (< 2.5 g/dL) driven by rapid trans-capillary extravasation into tissues and impaired liver synthesis.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, RT-PCR positive, viral RNA detection, molecular confirmation
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Reverse transcriptase-polymerase chain reaction detecting specific viral RNA in plasma within the first 1 to 10 days of symptoms.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, high viral load, Ct <20, high viraemia, poor prognosis
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Extremely high viral load (cycle threshold < 20 or > 10^7 copies/mL) on quantitative RT-PCR directly correlating with fatal outcome.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, antigen ELISA, nucleoprotein detection, early diagnosis
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Detection of circulating viral nucleoprotein or glycoprotein antigens in early acute serum prior to seroconversion.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, IgM capture ELISA, seroconversion, anti-viral antibody
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Detection of viral-specific IgM antibodies via capture ELISA around day 7 to 10 of illness, confirming acute or convalescent infection.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, cell culture isolation, BSL-4 biocontainment, live virus
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Successful culture and isolation of live virus in LLC-MK2 or Vero cell lines strictly requiring Biosafety Level 4 containment.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, no antibody response, fatal prognostic marker, immune failure
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Failure to mount detectable anti-viral IgG or neutralizing antibodies during the second week, a hallmark of fatal cases.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, IL-6, TNF-alpha, cytokine storm, systemic inflammation
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Massive surges of serum IL-6, IL-1, TNF-alpha, and interferon-gamma with suppressed IL-10 correlating with fatal DIC.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, RBC casts, hematuria, proteinuria, renal microvascular damage
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Urinalysis demonstrating dysmorphic red blood cells, RBC casts, and gross proteinuria indicative of glomerulotubular damage.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, confluent B-lines, interstitial syndrome, non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Point-of-care lung ultrasound revealing diffuse confluent B-lines and subpleural consolidations indicating non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, gallbladder edema, striated wall, capillary leak, acalculous cholecystitis
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Bedside abdominal ultrasound demonstrating gallbladder wall edema and stratification (> 3-4 mm) in the absence of gallstones (acalculous cholecystopathy).

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, pleural fluid, bilateral effusion, plasma leak, chest POCUS
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Ultrasound or chest radiography demonstrating bilateral anechoic fluid collections in pleural spaces secondary to capillary leakage.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, peritoneal fluid, Morrison pouch, ascites, third spacing
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Free fluid accumulation in Morrison's pouch and the pelvis visualized on point-of-care ultrasound reflecting third-spacing.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, pericardial fluid, echo stripe, serous effusion, myopericarditis
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Anechoic fluid stripe within the pericardial sac on focused cardiac ultrasound reflecting serous fluid extravasation.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, dilated bowel, paralytic ileus, static fluid, absent peristalsis
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Abdominal ultrasound revealing dilated, atonic, fluid-distended small and large bowel loops indicative of paralytic ileus.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, bright liver, diffuse steatosis, hepatocyte injury, viral hepatitis
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Ultrasound demonstrating increased hepatic echogenicity and attenuation reflecting diffuse microvesicular and macrovesicular steatosis.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, splenic enlargement, spleen length >13cm, reticuloendothelial congestion
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Splenic bipolar length exceeding 13 cm on bedside ultrasonography reflecting acute reticuloendothelial engorgement.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, interstitial haziness, ARDS, pulmonary infiltrates, chest x-ray
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Portable chest radiography revealing diffuse bilateral perihilar and interstitial haziness reflecting acute respiratory distress syndrome.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, human to human transmission, blood contact, vomitus, diarrhea, secondary spread
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Direct cutaneous or mucosal contact with blood, vomitus, diarrhea, saliva, or sweat of symptomatic VHF patients, driving explosive secondary transmission.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, burial rituals, washing deceased, corpse contact, peak viremia
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Traditional funeral and burial ceremonies involving direct physical contact, washing, or embracing deceased corpses retaining peak viral infectivity.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, needlestick, percutaneous inoculation, healthcare injury, high viral dose
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Accidental hollow-bore needlestick or sharp puncture during medical procedures, associated with rapid incubation and near-universal severe disease.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, nosocomial transmission, unsterilized equipment, needle reuse
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Reuse or improper sterilization of syringes, surgical instruments, and medical devices in low-resource healthcare settings causing nosocomial amplification.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, fruit bats, cave exposure, reservoir host, Marburg virus source
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Prolonged occupational or recreational exposure to subterranean mines, caves, or roosts inhabited by Egyptian fruit bats, the natural reservoir of Marburg virus.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, multimammate rat, rodent excreta, aerosolized dust, Lassa reservoir
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Ingestion of contaminated food or inhalation of aerosolized dust containing urine, feces, or saliva of the multimammate rat in West Africa, transmitting Lassa virus.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, tick bite, Hyalomma vector, CCHF transmission, pasture exposure
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Bite of infected adult Hyalomma marginatum marginatum ticks in scrubland, pastures, or agricultural fields transmitting CCHF virus.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, tick crushing, bare hand removal, percutaneous infection, CCHF
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Direct manual crushing of engorged ticks between bare fingers while grooming livestock, causing percutaneous viral inoculation of CCHF.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, livestock slaughter, sheep, cattle blood, abattoir contact, CCHF
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Direct contact with blood, viscera, or amniotic fluid of viraemic cattle, sheep, goats, or ostriches during slaughtering or shearing without personal protective equipment.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, mosquito bite, Aedes aegypti, urban transmission, Yellow fever
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Bites of urban and peri-domestic Aedes aegypti mosquitoes transmitting Yellow fever virus in tropical endemic regions of Africa and South America.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, canopy mosquito, forest vector, sylvatic cycle, Yellow fever
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Bites of canopy-dwelling Haemagogus mosquitoes responsible for transmitting sylvatic forest Yellow fever to tree-fellers and jungle workers.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, sexual transmission, viral persistence, semen shedding, survivor convalescence
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Unprotected sexual intercourse with male survivors up to several months after clinical recovery due to viral persistence in immunologically privileged testicular tubules.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, bushmeat, chimpanzee, gorilla, non-human primates, Ebola spillover
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Handling, butchering, or consuming carcass meat ('bushmeat') of chimpanzees, gorillas, or forest monkeys infected with Ebola or Marburg virus.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, healthcare workers, nosocomial risk, doctors, nurses, barrier precautions
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Doctors, nurses, and hospital cleaners caring for actively hemorrhaging or vomiting patients without specialized barrier personal protective equipment.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, abattoir workers, butchers, animal slaughter, occupational hazard
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Butchery and slaughterhouse personnel handling fresh carcasses and blood of livestock in CCHF-endemic pastoral zones.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, farmers, agricultural workers, rural endemic zone, animal husbandry
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Agricultural workers, shepherds, and cattle handlers residing in rural endemic areas with frequent Hyalomma tick encounters.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, miners, cave workers, bat colonies, subterranean shafts
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Artisanal miners entering gold or cobalt subterranean caves harboring dense colonies of Rousettus fruit bats.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, pregnancy, obstetric hemorrhage, maternal mortality, placental tropism
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Expectant mothers experiencing severe immune modulation, placental viral amplification, massive obstetric hemorrhage, and near 90% fetal wastage.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, laboratory technicians, laboratory acquired infection, biosafety risk
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Laboratory scientists and technicians processing viable clinical specimens without full positive-pressure BSL-4 protective suites.

relationships.keywords: INCUBATION_PERIOD, filovirus incubation, 2-21 days, symptom onset window
relationships.description: [INCUBATION_PERIOD] Classical incubation window for filovirus infections (Ebola and Marburg) ranging from 2 to 21 days (most commonly 5 to 10 days).

relationships.keywords: INCUBATION_PERIOD, CCHF incubation, tick bite incubation, 1-9 days, rapid onset
relationships.description: [INCUBATION_PERIOD] Rapid incubation period of CCHF following a tick bite (average 1 to 3 days, maximum 9 days; extending to 5 to 13 days after blood exposure).

relationships.keywords: INCUBATION_PERIOD, Lassa incubation, 6-21 days, insidious onset, rodent contact
relationships.description: [INCUBATION_PERIOD] Prolonged insidious incubation period of Lassa fever typically spanning 6 to 21 days following rodent excreta contact.

relationships.keywords: INCUBATION_PERIOD, Yellow fever incubation, 3-6 days, mosquito bite to fever
relationships.description: [INCUBATION_PERIOD] Short, rapid incubation period of Yellow fever spanning 3 to 6 days between mosquito bite and acute prodrome onset.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, no travel history, non-endemic, 21 days window, exclusion rule
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Complete absence of travel to, residence in, or contact with visitors from VHF-endemic regions within the preceding 21 days definitively excludes acute VHF.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, chronic illness, duration >4 weeks, indolent course, exclusion rule
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Illness duration extending continuously beyond 3 to 4 weeks prior to initial presentation is clinically incompatible with acute fulminant VHF.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, normal platelets >150000, preserved thrombocytes, exclusion rule
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Completely normal platelet count (> 150,000/uL) throughout the acute toxic febrile illness reliably excludes acute VHF.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, thrombocytosis >450000, elevated platelets, reactive process
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Platelet count exceeding 450,000/uL indicates a reactive bacterial process or myeloproliferative disorder, completely incompatible with VHF.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, normal PT, normal aPTT, intact coagulation, exclusion rule
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Entirely normal PT/INR, aPTT, and fibrinogen levels in a severely toxic febrile patient rules out acute viral hemorrhagic diathesis.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, antibiotic response, defervescence on cephalosporin, bacterial cure
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Rapid defervescence and hemodynamic stabilization within 24 to 48 hours of empirical broad-spectrum antibacterial therapy rules out VHF.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, procalcitonin >10, bacterial biomarker, sepsis, exclusion rule
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Extremely high procalcitonin levels (> 10 ng/mL) at presentation strongly favor severe bacterial sepsis rather than primary uncomplicated VHF.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, malaria smear positive, Plasmodium falciparum, intraerythrocytic parasites
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Detection of intraerythrocytic Plasmodium falciparum ring forms and trophozoites establishes malaria as the primary etiology.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, lobar pneumonia, dense consolidation, bacterial airspace disease
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Dense unilateral lobar airspace consolidation on chest radiography indicates bacterial pneumonia rather than VHF.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, normal lymphocyte count, preserved lymphocytes, no apoptosis
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Normal or elevated absolute lymphocyte count during days 1 to 3 of high fever is highly atypical for the severe lymphoid depletion of VHF.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, normal AST, normal ALT, absence of liver injury, exclusion rule
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Completely normal serum AST and ALT levels in an acutely deteriorating patient rules out hepatic-tropic viral hemorrhagic fevers.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, normal ferritin, ferritin <300, absence of cytokine storm
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Serum ferritin level within standard reference limits (< 300 ng/mL) during acute toxic fever strongly contradicts VHF hyperferritinemic storm.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, itchy rash, urticaria, wheals, allergic reaction, non-VHF rash
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Itchy wheals and pruritic urticaria indicate allergic or parasitic etiology, contrasting with the non-pruritic maculopapular rash of VHF.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, purulent eye discharge, crusting, bacterial conjunctivitis
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Copious purulent eye discharge and crusting indicates bacterial conjunctivitis rather than the dry, injected suffusion of VHF.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, early leukocytosis, WBC >15000 day 1, bacterial infection
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] High neutrophilia (> 15,000/uL) on day 1 of fever without prior leukopenia points toward acute pyogenic bacterial infection.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, massive splenomegaly, chronic hypersplenism, visceral leishmaniasis
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Massive firm splenomegaly present for months indicates chronic tropical splenomegaly, visceral leishmaniasis, or cirrhosis.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, bacteremia, blood culture positive, Neisseria meningitidis
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Growth of pathogenic bacteria (e.g., Neisseria meningitidis, Salmonella enterica) identifies primary pyogenic bacteremia.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, negative PCR day 4, undetectable viral RNA, definitive exclusion
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Negative reverse transcriptase-PCR on an adequate plasma sample collected on or after day 4 of symptoms reliably rules out active VHF viremia.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, lactate <1.5, normal tissue perfusion, non-VHF shock
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Normal blood lactate (< 1.5 mmol/L) in a patient presenting with shock contradicts the severe microcirculatory hypoperfusion of VHF.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, isolated hematuria, normal platelets, nephrolithiasis, non-VHF
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Microscopic or gross hematuria with normal platelet count and normal clotting screen points to urological disease rather than VHF.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, gallbladder wall <2mm, intact endothelium, no third spacing
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Completely thin normal gallbladder wall (< 2 mm) without pericholecystic fluid argues against severe capillary leak syndrome.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, artemisinin cure, malaria response, fever clearance
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Rapid clinical recovery and fever clearance following antimalarial therapy confirms uncomplicated malaria.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, plasma leakage timing, defervescence, lack of nosocomial spread, lower AST
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Contrasted with Severe Dengue, which exhibits plasma leakage strictly timed to defervescence (days 3-7) and transaminases rarely exceeding 1,000 U/L, whereas VHF causes catastrophic early transaminitis (AST:ALT > 3:1, AST > 2,000-10,000 U/L) and person-to-person transmission.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, blood smear parasitemia, artesunate response, lack of person-to-person spread
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Contrasted with Falciparum Malaria, which presents with cyclical rigors, high intraerythrocytic parasitemia on peripheral blood smear, rapid therapeutic clearance with intravenous artesunate, and lacks human-to-human body fluid infectivity.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, day-1 leukocytosis, direct hyperbilirubinemia, calf tenderness, penicillin response
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Contrasted with Leptospirosis, which features marked day-1 neutrophilic leukocytosis, deep direct hyperbilirubinemia, severe calf muscle tenderness, and prompt bactericidal response to intravenous penicillin or ceftriaxone.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, step-ladder fever, positive blood culture, lack of early DIC, normal platelets early
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Contrasted with Typhoid Fever, which manifests step-ladder fever, rose spots, relative bradycardia, and positive blood cultures for Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi, lacking profound early thrombocytopenia and fulminant DIC.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, purpura fulminans, high procalcitonin, ceftriaxone response, CSF pleocytosis
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Contrasted with Meningococcemia, which presents with explosive purpura fulminans, neutrophilic cerebrospinal fluid pleocytosis, rapid response to third-generation cephalosporins, and elevated procalcitonin (> 10 ng/mL).

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, focal pyogenic source, high procalcitonin, rapid response to antibiotics
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Contrasted with Acute Bacterial Sepsis, which demonstrates identifiable focal pyogenic sources (pneumonia, pyelonephritis), marked procalcitonin elevation, and hemodynamic stabilization upon targeted antibacterial administration.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, inoculation eschar, doxycycline response, centripetal rash, intracellular bacteria
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Contrasted with Rickettsial Disease (e.g., epidemic typhus, Rocky Mountain spotted fever), which characteristically features an inoculation eschar, centripetal rash, and rapid therapeutic response within 48 hours to oral or intravenous doxycycline.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, ALT > AST, absence of consumptive DIC, absence of severe early shock
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Contrasted with Acute Viral Hepatitis (hepatitis A, B, or E), where transaminitis is heavily ALT-predominant (ALT >> AST), whereas VHF features profound AST-dominant transaminitis (AST:ALT > 3:1 to 5:1) with severe thrombocytopenia.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, fecal leukocytes, fluoroquinolone response, absence of endothelial shock
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Contrasted with Shigellosis, which causes acute inflammatory dysentery with high fecal leukocytes and mucosal ulceration responding to fluoroquinolones, without systemic endothelial destruction, DIC, or transaminitis.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, localized right lower quadrant signs, normal platelet count, intact coagulation
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Contrasted with Acute Appendicitis, which causes localized right lower quadrant peritoneal signs with normal platelets and coagulation, whereas VHF abdominal pain represents diffuse mucosal ischemia and microvascular hemorrhage.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, schistocytes, normal PT aPTT, ADAMTS13 deficiency, plasma exchange response
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Contrasted with Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura (TTP), which exhibits prominent microangiopathic hemolytic anemia with abundant schistocytes and normal PT/aPTT, unlike the consumptive DIC with prolonged coagulation tests in VHF.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, isolated thrombocytopenia, normal liver enzymes, intact coagulation, afebrile
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Contrasted with Immune Thrombocytopenic Purpura (ITP), which presents with isolated immune-mediated thrombocytopenia with entirely normal liver enzymes, normal clotting times, and absence of systemic toxic fever.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, Faget sign, Councilman bodies, 17D vaccine protection, Flaviviridae
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Contrasted with other filovirus and bunyavirus VHFs, Yellow Fever is an endemic flavivirus distinguished by Faget sign (marked sphygmothermic dissociation), midzonal hepatic Councilman bodies, deep early jaundice, and prevention via the live-attenuated 17D vaccine.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, exudative pharyngitis, 8th-nerve deafness, Mastomys reservoir, ribavirin response
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Contrasted with filovirus infections, Lassa Fever is an arenavirus endemic to West Africa featuring prominent exudative pharyngitis, retrosternal pain, eighth-nerve sensorineural deafness, and clinical responsiveness to early intravenous ribavirin.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, Hyalomma tick vector, livestock exposure, severe backache, ribavirin sensitivity
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Contrasted with mosquito-borne or bat-borne VHFs, CCHF is a tick-borne nairovirus associated with Hyalomma ticks and livestock contact across Eurasia, presenting with extreme lumbosacral pain and responsive to ribavirin therapy.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, Rousettus bat reservoir, up to 88% mortality, lack of ribavirin response, Filoviridae
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Contrasted with bunyavirus and arenavirus fevers, Marburg Virus Disease is a filovirus linked to Rousettus fruit bat caves and direct body fluid contact, characterized by up to 88% case fatality and complete lack of response to ribavirin.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, predominant pulmonary failure, lack of overt bleeding, New World rodents
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Contrasted with pantropic hemorrhagic fevers, HPS presents primarily with non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema, severe hypoxia, hemoconcentration, and minimal hemorrhagic diathesis following New World rodent excreta inhalation.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, suppurative buboes, safety-pin Gram stain, Yersinia pestis, aminoglycoside response
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Contrasted with Plague (bubonic/septicemic Yersinia pestis), which presents with acutely suppurative regional lymph nodes (buboes), Gram-negative bipolar safety-pin bacilli on microscopy, and prompt clinical cure with aminoglycosides or doxycycline.
